title: HTTP API server surface (read-only, Tailscale-bound, bearer-token)
context:
Operator directive 2026-09-23: V2-068 lands 'API-first, MCP-second' as a typed-Python-module + a streamable-HTTP MCP server. But there's a third audience the MCP transport doesn't cover cleanly: external HTTP integrations (n8n, Home Assistant, debugging scripts, Grafana, ad-hoc curl during outages). MCP-over-streamable-HTTP works for AI agents but is awkward for scripting + dashboards. This PRD adds a parallel HTTP API server (separate process, separate port) that exposes the same `infra.farm_api.*` resource groups as plain JSON REST. Strictly read-only. Auth and bind rules mirror the MCP server so operators only learn one security model.

This is the third service in a three-process architecture:
  - Listener `:8090`   — Reolink webhook ingest, alert pipeline (existing, V2-049+).
  - API server `:8092` — read-only JSON HTTP, THIS PRD, GET routes only.
  - MCP server `:8091` — read-only JSON-RPC / streamable-HTTP for AI clients (V2-068).

Each process has its own PID, its own logs, its own restart story. They share the filesystem (`data/state/`, `data/events/`, `~/.env`) but no shared memory. A crash in API does NOT stop alerts. A crash in MCP does NOT stop the listener.
shipping_definition: New process `infra/api_server.py` — stdlib `http.server.HTTPServer` + `BaseHTTPRequestHandler` (no Flask dep; the MCP server pattern already proves stdlib suffices for read-only multi-threaded services). Daemon-threadable so a launchd plist can call it as a singleton.

Binds to `:8092` by default, override via `FARMSURV_API_PORT`. Binds to Tailscale (100.64.0.0/10) by default, override via `FARMSURV_API_BIND=tailnet-only|all|<interface>` (mirror V2-068 binding contract; reuse `_resolve_bind_address()` from `infra/mcp_server.py` if possible, factor out into `infra/net_bind.py` as part of US-072a1).
Bearer-token auth required: env `FARMSURV_API_TOKEN` (≥32 chars). Reject with HTTP 401 if missing or wrong. Same abort-at-startup pattern as MCP server.
GET /healthz                                -> {ok: true, box_id, uptime_seconds, api_enabled, started_at}
GET /api/v1/cameras                        -> list of CameraInfo (delegates to infra.farm_api.cameras.list_cameras)
(Total 17 routes — one per MCP tool + healthz. Add new routes only when adding new farm_api functions.)

Listener-spawn hook: when `FARMSURV_API_ENABLED=1`, `listener/daemon.py` spawns `infra.api_server.run()` on a daemon thread at boot. Same pattern as US-068g1 will define for MCP. Both processes spawnable independently: enable API without MCP, MCP without API, both, or neither.
Existing `infra/farm_api/*` modules are reused as-is — no changes to the typed Python contract.
All knobs env-tunable, listed in `.env.example` with the 1=ON/0=OFF convention comment per AGENTS.md.

Existing 178 unit + 17 e2e tests + 16 MCP tests continue to pass. New tests: 17 route tests (one per route) + 1 healthz + 4 auth tests (token missing / wrong / valid / too short) + 1 bind-refusal test = ≥23 new tests.

Live verification per AGENTS.md Step 2: spawn listener (Python subprocess), wait 5s, curl `:8092/healthz` with bearer token, assert JSON shape matches; curl `:8092/api/v1/gate`, assert presence of `night_suppress_cameras` field; curl without bearer, assert HTTP 401.
Forgejo mirror pushed after merge to main (US-068e auto-push hook covers this).
design_principles: Reuse `infra.farm_api.*` verbatim. Routes are 3-line adapters — exactly the same pattern as MCP tools in V2-068. If we ever change the typed Python contract, both transports move in lockstep because they're parsed from the same dataclasses.
Mirror MCP's security model, don't innovate. Bearer token from env, abort-at-startup if missing/short, Tailscale-only bind, HTTP 401 on bad token. One policy, one docs page. Operators learn it once.
Three-process architecture. API crashes do not affect listener (alert pipeline) or MCP (agent clients). Each has independent restart cadence, independent launchd entry, independent log file.
No write routes in this PRD. Mute-camera, enroll-identity, set-cooldown, restart-listener are V2-073 (write surface). This PRD scopes read-only explicitly.

Cross-process filesystem is the contract. API reads `data/state/`, `data/events/`, `data/frames/{camera}/{alert_id}/event.json`. Same paths the listener writes. No shared memory, no shared DB connection, no live pipeline coupling. Stale-by-design (within last 24h) is acceptable — caller can retry.

Bind mirror: factor `_resolve_bind_address()` out of `infra/mcp_server.py:583` into `infra/net_bind.py:resolve_bind_address()` and reuse from both `infra/mcp_server.py` and `infra/api_server.py`. Single source of truth for Tailscale-bound semantics.

deployment_modes.single_host: All three processes on the Mac mini (current deployment). Listeners on `:8090`, API on `:8092`, MCP on `:8091`.
deployment_modes.split_api: Listener stays on Mac mini. API server moves to a Tailscale-attached Linux box that mounts the same Synology NAS. Listen on `:8092` pointed at the NAS — read-only filesystem mounts are sufficient for the API surface since the contract is read-mostly.
deployment_modes.split_mcp: API server + listener co-located. MCP server moves to a Tailscale-attached Linux box with `infra/mcp_server.py` reading from NAS. The MCP server needs read access to `data/state/` and `data/events/` only.
deployment_modes.full_split: All three processes on different hosts, sharing the Synology NAS as the only filesystem coupling. Auth tokens rotate per process; `FARMSURV_*_BOX_ID` identifies which host each query originated from.

stories.title: infra/net_bind.py: shared Tailscale-binding helper (factor out from mcp_server.py:583)
scope: Create `infra/net_bind.py:resolve_bind_address(spec: str) -> str` — accepts 'tailnet-only', 'all', or a literal interface name. Returns the bind address string. Lifts the body of `_resolve_bind_address()` in `infra/mcp_server.py:583` verbatim, with proper docstring.
Add `infra/net_bind.py:is_tailnet_ip(addr: str) -> bool` helper. Detects 100.64.0.0/10.
Re-export from `infra/net_bind` so `infra.mcp_server` and `infra.api_server` both `from infra.net_bind import resolve_bind_address, is_tailnet_ip`.
Update `infra/mcp_server.py:_resolve_bind_address()` to delegate to the new helper. Existing behavior unchanged. Existing 16 MCP tests continue to pass.

Add `tests/test_net_bind.py` covering: 'tailnet-only' resolves to a 100.x address; 'all' resolves to '0.0.0.0'; literal interface name resolves to that interface's IP; raises ValueError on unknown spec.

stories.title: infra/api_server.py: HTTP API server (read-only, bearer-token, Tailscale-only)
scope: New module `infra/api_server.py` — stdlib `http.server.HTTPServer` + `ThreadingMixIn` + `BaseHTTPRequestHandler`. Mirrors `infra/mcp_server.py:611` shape.
Class `_APIHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler)` with `do_GET()` — dispatches by URL path to a `_ROUTES` dict mapping path-prefix → callables.
Bearer-token middleware in `_APIHandler._check_auth()` — exact same logic as `infra/mcp_server.py` (validate `Authorization: Bearer {token}` against `FARMSURV_API_TOKEN`, HTTP 401 on miss).

Each route is a 3-line adapter — calls the underlying `infra.farm_api.*` function, serializes via `dataclasses.asdict()`, returns JSON. Binary routes (`get_camera_snapshot`) return raw PNG bytes with `Content-Type: image/png`.
`/healthz` route returns `{ok: true, box_id, uptime_seconds, api_enabled, started_at}` — mirrors MCP server `/healthz` schema.

Function `run() -> None` — reads `FARMSURV_API_ENABLED`, `FARMSURV_API_PORT`, `FARMSURV_API_BIND`, `FARMSURV_API_TOKEN`, aborts if `FARMSURV_API_ENABLED=1` and token missing or shorter than 32 chars. Mirrors `infra/mcp_server.py:643`.
Bind via `infra.net_bind.resolve_bind_address()`. Same Tailscale-only default.
Add to `infra/__init__.py` exports.
Add `.env.example` entries with the 1=ON/0=OFF convention comment per AGENTS.md Step 3.

Add `tests/test_api_server.py` with: 17 route tests (one per documented route), 1 healthz test, 4 auth tests (missing/wrong/valid/short), 1 bind-refusal test = ≥23 tests. Use `urllib.request` (same pattern as `tests/test_mcp_server.py`).
env_knobs: FARMSURV_API_TOKEN (no default; required when FARMSURV_API_ENABLED=1; ≥32 chars)

stories.title: listener/daemon.py: spawn API server on daemon thread when FARMSURV_API_ENABLED=1
scope: In `listener/daemon.py:bootstrap()` — after MCP server spawn hook (US-068g1), check `FARMSURV_API_ENABLED`. If 1, spawn `infra.api_server.run()` on a daemon thread. Log `{event: 'api_server_spawned', port, bind_address}`.
Same thread + log pattern as MCP server spawn.
Add `tests/test_daemon_api_spawn.py` — spawn listener subprocess in test mode, wait 5s, curl `:8092/healthz` with bearer token (test-mode sets a known token), assert JSON shape. Tear down at end.

Live verification per AGENTS.md Step 2 — operator restart needed before this takes effect on PID 51669. Pre-populated `.env` carries `FARMSURV_API_ENABLED=0` (default), so a manual operator-driven `FARMSURV_API_ENABLED=1` is the next step after merge. Documented as a follow-up, not part of shipping_definition.

stories.title: docs/API.md: document HTTP routes + auth + bind model
scope: Add a new section 'HTTP API (cross-process)' at the top of `docs/API.md` covering: routes (path, method, returns, example curl), auth (bearer token env name), bind model (Tailscale-only), how to enable (FARMSURV_API_ENABLED=1 + token), deployment modes (single-host, split-api, split-mcp, full-split).
Cross-reference: API surface mirrors MCP tools 1:1 — when MCP gets a new tool, API gets a new route. Document the rule.
Cross-reference: V2-068 PRD for MCP transport, V2-072 PRD for HTTP transport; both back to the same `infra.farm_api.*` typed Python contract.

constraints: No new runtime dependencies. Use stdlib (http.server, urllib.request, json, threading) the same way `infra/mcp_server.py` does. Adding Flask/FastAPI/Starlette would force a venv rebuild and a separate dep-tree audit; out of scope.
No write routes in this PRD. Mute-camera, enroll-identity, set-cooldown, restart-listener are explicitly V2-073 (write surface). The API surface remains strictly read-only.
Bind / auth / token rules are MIRRORED from V2-068. Do not introduce a new security policy. Operators learn one model.

No shared state with listener. The API reads the filesystem (`data/state/`, `data/events/`, `data/frames/`) the same way the MCP server does. Read-only is the contract; cross-process file reads are fine, file writes are forbidden.

Listener restart on production requires operator approval per AGENTS.md Step 2.1 / Step 4. After merge, operator must restart before the API server is reachable on PID 51669. Document this; do not auto-restart the listener.
Card body soft limit 2,500 chars, operational ceiling ~4,500 per AGENTS.md Step 5. Decompose further if any card exceeds this.
Forgejo mirror pushed after merge. US-068e auto-push hook (just shipped) covers this PRD's branches automatically.
open_questions: Should the API server log requests at INFO or DEBUG level? INFO = ops visibility, DEBUG = noise. Default INFO; the API logs request path + response status, never request body (we don't auth via POST yet, but be ready).

Should the API server emit a `box_id` per response (per `FARMSURV_BOX_ID` env var, default 'test-box-01'/'unidentified') so callers can tell which physical host returned the JSON? Useful in split-deployment mode. Default: yes for `/healthz`, optional elsewhere.
Should the API server support CORS? Probably no for v1 — call from server-side scripts only. Browser dashboards would need a CORS layer; defer until a real browser dashboard ships.
Rate limiting? Currently no. Tailscale-only bind means LAN-side brute force isn't a vector. Add if a public-internet deployment becomes a future ask (V2-074?).
